## First run

<Steps>

1. Fill in `apps/api/.env` (database, Redis, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, SMTP) and
   give `apps/worker/.env` the same `DATABASE_URL` and `REDIS_*`.

2. Start Postgres and Redis, and wait until they accept connections:

   ```sh
   yarn dc:up && yarn dc:wait
   ```

3. Create the first migration and seed:

   ```sh
   yarn db:migrate --name init
   yarn db:seed
   ```

4. Run every app:

   ```sh
   yarn dev        # the API on http://localhost:5000/docs, plus the worker
   ```

</Steps>

## Commands

From the root, turbo runs each across every workspace, building `@scope/db`
first:

```sh
yarn build | typecheck | lint | test
yarn format
```

One workspace: `yarn workspace @scope/api <script>`, or the script from the
app's folder.

## Changing the schema

<Steps>

1. Edit `packages/db/prisma/schema/*.prisma`.

2. From the root or `apps/api`:

   ```sh
   yarn db:migrate --name add_things
   ```

   This runs `prisma migrate dev` in `@scope/db` with the API's `.env`, then
   rebuilds the client.

3. Restart `yarn dev`, and run `yarn typecheck` from the root: it checks every
   app against the new client at once.

</Steps>

<Aside title="Tests use db push">
The API's test database is pushed, not migrated: `yarn test:db:push` from
`apps/api` after a schema change. It runs `prisma db push --accept-data-loss`,
which Prisma refuses to run from an AI agent without the user's explicit
consent.
</Aside>

## Tests

The API's suites, as in [nest-api](../../nest-api/development/), run from
`apps/api` against `compose.test.yml` (ports 5499 / 6399):

```sh
cd apps/api
yarn test:dc:reinstall    # once: test stack up, schema pushed, seeded
yarn test                 # unit
yarn test:e2e             # e2e
```
